title: Slice a cucumber on a mandoline with its hand guard, holding the mandoline steady, then slide out the tray of slices
instruction: Slice the cucumber on the mandoline using its hand guard: hold the mandoline steady by its handle with one hand while the other slides the red hand guard, which holds the cucumber, down the deck across the blade and back up, four times. Never bring a gripper near the blade itself. Then leave the guard at the top of the deck, slide the tray of slices out from under the mandoline by its pull tab, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: A mandoline's blade takes off fingertips as easily as cucumber, so the food is pushed with the hand guard, never by hand, while the other hand holds the mandoline by its handle: pushed without it being held, a mandoline slides away on the worktop and nothing gets cut.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A mandoline slicer (0.7 kg) standing on the table, its deck running left to right: a brushed stainless-steel deck 11 cm wide and 30 cm long, rising 15 degrees toward the left, its lower end 3.6 cm above the table at 32 cm forward and 19 cm right of the centre line; black ABS rails 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall along both edges and black end caps; a slanted steel blade across the deck 9.5 cm up from its lower end, in a dark slot; two black rubber feet under the lower end, 14.8 cm apart; a folding steel wire leg under the deck 24 cm up; and beyond the upper end a black ABS loop handle 9.5 cm long (two square side bars 1.6 cm thick, 8 cm apart, joined at the end). Its feet are smooth (friction 0.12-0.15), so it slides on the table when pushed with about 1 N. (2) On the deck, a red ABS hand guard 7.5 cm along the deck, 9.6 cm wide and 3.6 cm tall, with a square knob 2.2 cm across and 2.6 cm tall on top and a round window showing the cucumber inside; its middle starts 20 cm up the deck. A chunk of cucumber 4 cm across stands in it on its cut end. The guard rides in the rails: it slides along the deck (from 4.5 to 24.5 cm up it) when pushed with more than about 2.5 N, and stays where it is left. (3) A white polypropylene tray 9.4 cm wide, 13 cm long and 1.8 cm deep, under the lower half of the mandoline and its blade, its middle 32 cm forward and 11 cm right of the centre line, with a pull tab sticking out 6.5 cm past the mandoline's lower end to the right (a low bar ending in a grip 2.5 cm long and 2.8 cm tall). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. A slice is cut each time the guard is slid from more than 15 cm up the deck (its middle) to less than 7.8 cm up it, pushing the cucumber across the blade; it drops from under the blade. A slice is in the tray when its middle lies within the tray's walls. The tray is slid out once it has moved 10 cm or more toward the right. The guard is at the top of the deck when its middle is 16 cm or more up the deck. The mandoline is steady when it ends within 3 cm of where it started, tilted 10 degrees or less. 0.0 once a gripper's TCP (the point between its fingertips) has come within 3 cm of the blade's edge, at any time. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 with at least four slices in the tray, the tray slid out, the guard at the top of the deck, the mandoline steady and both arms back where they started (each gripper's TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.75 with at least four slices in the tray and the tray slid out; 0.5 with at least four slices in the tray; 0.25 with two or three; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the mandoline, the guard and the tray still.
reset_notes: Slide the guard back to 20 cm up the deck, take the slices out of the tray and slide the tray back under the mandoline.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the guard rides on a joint along the deck and is held where it is left with up to 2.5 N (rails and blade); the cucumber is part of the guard and does not get shorter; slicing is a rule: each completed pass drops a ready-made slice, kept out of sight under the table until then, from under the blade. No cutting is simulated. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
